# osc_parameter_store (Resource)

Manages a parameter store, the source of a My App's environment variables. Bind an app to it with `config_service` on `osc_my_app`, and manage its values with `osc_parameter`.

This is not the same as an `osc_instance` of `eyevinn-app-config-svc`: the platform creates the store with an encryption key and an API key it keeps as secrets, so secret values can be stored and a bound app can decrypt them.

Destroying the store deletes every value in it, and the Valkey instance OSC created for it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A parameter store for an app's environment. OSC creates a Valkey instance for it
# and holds its encryption and API keys, so it can store secrets.
resource "osc_parameter_store" "api" {
  name = "myapiconfig"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Store name: letters and digits only. Changing it replaces the store.

### Optional

- `enable_secrets` (Boolean) Create the store with an encryption key and an API key, so that it can hold secret values. Changing it replaces the store.
- `redis_url` (String, Sensitive) Valkey or Redis URL to keep the values in. When unset OSC creates a Valkey instance for the store, which is the usual choice. Changing it replaces the store.

### Read-Only

- `config_api_key` (String, Sensitive) The store's API key, which reads secret values in plain text. Empty when secrets are disabled.
- `id` (String) The store name. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `url` (String) URL of the store's API.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import osc_parameter_store.api myapiconfig
```
